item.title: Moving to Lakeview: Six-Flats, Game Days, and Why People Stay
item.description:
What Lakeview is actually like to live in. Courtyard six-flats, the Wrigley Field effect on daily life, why so many people arrive for one year and stay for nine, and the late-August week when the whole neighborhood turns over at once.

Covers ZIP codes 60613 and 60657.

item.title: Moving to Lincoln Park: The Park, DePaul, and 34-Inch Stairwells
item.description:
What Lincoln Park is actually like to live in. Over 1,200 acres of lakefront park with a free zoo, the DePaul calendar that drives the whole neighborhood every August and May, and a housing stock that runs from narrow brownstone walk-ups to high-rises on the Drive.

Covers ZIP code 60614.

item.title: Moving to the Gold Coast: Why You Can't Move on a Saturday
item.description:
The Gold Coast is the one Chicago neighborhood where your move date isn't entirely your decision. Freight elevator windows that exclude weekends, limestone mansions on Astor with staircases built for a different era of furniture, and why January through March is the clearest stretch of the year here.

Covers ZIP codes 60610 and 60611.

item.title: Moving to Old Town Chicago: Carriage Houses, Wells Street, and Narrow Alleys
item.description:
What Old Town is actually like to live in. Carriage houses hidden behind main-street addresses, 1870s two-flats sitting next to 1990s townhomes on the same block, the split personality of Wells Street versus the side streets, and alleys that vary from truck-friendly to impassable.

Covers ZIP codes 60610 and 60614.

item.title: Moving to Andersonville: Glogg, Pine Stairs, and Market Saturdays
item.description:

Covers ZIP code 60640.

item.title: Moving to Uptown: Charlie Chaplin, Jazz, and Very Long Hallways
item.description:

Covers ZIP code 60640.

item.title: Moving to Edgewater: Two Neighborhoods in Three Blocks
item.description:

Covers ZIP code 60660.

item.title: Moving to Ravenswood: The Train Runs Through It
item.description:
The Brown Line runs elevated straight through the middle of Ravenswood, so train noise is part of the deal. In exchange you get one of the easiest neighborhoods in the city to move in and out of, plus loft conversions in the old industrial corridor.

Covers ZIP codes 60613 and 60625.

item.title: Moving to Lincoln Square: Maifest, Oktoberfest, and the Folk School
item.description:

Covers ZIP codes 60618 and 60625.

item.title: Moving to Roscoe Village: The Trade You Make for Quiet

Covers ZIP codes 60618 and 60657.
